articles.title: Jovem fica cinco dias à espera de vaga em CTI após acidente de moto no Sul de MG | G1
articles.standfirst: Matheus Henrique Santos Vicente está internado desde domingo (18), em Varginha, após sofrer um forte impacto na cabeça. A transferência para um hospital em Divinópolis foi autorizada nesta sexta-feira (23).
articles.summary: Matheus Henrique Santos Vicente está internado desde domingo (18), em Varginha, após sofrer um forte impacto na cabeça. A transferência para um hospital em Divinópolis foi autorizada nesta sexta-feira (23).
articles.body:
Um jovem de 27 anos ficou cinco dias à espera de uma vaga em um Centro de Terapia Intensiva (CTI) após sofrer um acidente de motocicleta e bater a cabeça em Varginha (MG). Matheus Henrique Santos Vicente está internado desde domingo (18) no Hospital Bom Pastor. A transferência para o Hospital São João de Deus, em Divinópolis, no Centro-Oeste de Minas, foi autorizada na manhã desta sexta-feira (23), segundo a Secretaria de Estado de Saúde de Minas Gerais (SES-MG).

Durante os dias de espera, a família cobrou agilidade na transferência e demonstrou preocupação com a demora para conseguir um leito com suporte neurológico especializado.

“Desde domingo, a gente está aqui correndo atrás, com a zona de risco que o meu irmão está aqui, lutando pela vida. E está tendo um pouco de descaso aqui, cada vez fala uma coisa”, afirmou David Dário Vicente, irmão de Matheus.

O familiar também questionou a falta de informações claras sobre os critérios para a liberação da vaga e disse que a família não sabia mais a quem recorrer. “A gente está sem saber o que faz mais, quem a gente corre atrás, quem vai ajudar a gente”, desabafou.

Matheus Henrique Santos Vicente está internado desde domingo (18) no Hospital Bom Pastor, em Varginha (MG) — Foto: Reprodução EPTV

Segundo os familiares, Matheus sofreu o acidente em uma curva da Avenida Perimetral, nas proximidades da Fazenda Experimental, em Varginha. Ele teria perdido o controle da motocicleta durante a manobra, caído e sofrido um forte impacto na cabeça.

De acordo com os parentes, o capacete que o jovem usava chegou a se romper com a força da batida. Desde então, ele permanece na sala de emergência do Hospital Bom Pastor, sob cuidados médicos e monitoramento contínuo.

A equipe médica identificou a necessidade de transferência para um CTI com suporte neurológico especializado.

Em nota, a Secretaria de Estado de Saúde informou que a Central de Regulação de Leitos (CORE Saúde MG) realizou tentativas de transferência desde o primeiro dia de cadastro do paciente no sistema estadual.

Segundo a SES-MG, seis hospitais foram consultados: Hospital Regional do Sul de Minas, Hospital Universitário Alzira Velano, Santa Casa Paraíso, Santa Casa de Misericórdia de Lavras, Hospital das Clínicas Samuel Libânio e Hospital São João de Deus. De acordo com a secretaria, não havia leito adequado disponível nas unidades durante as tentativas anteriores.

O órgão explicou que a regulação considera a necessidade clínica do paciente, o perfil de atendimento exigido, as referências de assistência para cada região e a disponibilidade de leitos. A secretaria ressaltou que a prioridade é garantir o acesso ao serviço adequado em tempo oportuno.

Transporte será providenciado pelo hospital

A transferência de Matheus para o Hospital São João de Deus, em Divinópolis, foi autorizada na manhã desta sexta-feira (23). Segundo a SES-MG, o transporte deve ser providenciado pelo Hospital Bom Pastor, onde o jovem está internado.

Em posicionamento divulgado antes da autorização, a Fundação Hospitalar do Município de Varginha (FHOMUV), responsável pelo Hospital Bom Pastor, informou que o paciente recebia cuidados ininterruptos e monitoramento contínuo na sala de emergência.

A instituição afirmou que a solicitação havia sido cadastrada no sistema estadual e que a definição do hospital de destino dependia da regulação estadual do SUS.

A Secretaria Municipal de Saúde de Varginha informou que mantinha contato com a FHOMUV para contribuir com os encaminhamentos necessários à continuidade da assistência ao paciente, em articulação com a regulação estadual.

articles.title: Vigilâncias Sanitária e Epidemiológica fazem inspeção em hospital de SP após mortes de bebês | G1
articles.standfirst: As crianças de zero a três anos teriam morrido por consequência de infecções hospitalares. Unidade diz que está à disposição das autoridades e já atendeu mais de 100 mil crianças nos últimos meses.
articles.summary: As crianças de zero a três anos teriam morrido por consequência de infecções hospitalares. Unidade diz que está à disposição das autoridades e já atendeu mais de 100 mil crianças nos últimos meses.
articles.body:
Os Centros de Vigilância Sanitária (CVS) e de Vigilância Epidemiológica (CVE) do Estado de São Paulo realizaram nesta sexta-feira (23), em conjunto com a Vigilância Epidemiológica Municipal, uma inspeção no Hospital Salvalus, na Mooca, Zona Leste de São Paulo, após a divulgação de mortes de bebês na instituição neste ano.

As vigilâncias dizem avaliar as circunstâncias de 35 óbitos de bebês registrados neste ano . A Polícia Civil investiga a morte de seis bebês no hospital, que rtence à rede Hapvida, do grupo NotreDame Intermédica. (leia mais abaixo).

As equipes avaliaram as condições de funcionamento das unidades neonatal e pediátrica, os protocolos de higienização e prevenção de infecções e o monitoramento dos indicadores assistenciais. Também analisaram as mudanças no perfil de atendimento, especialmente em relação aos pacientes de alta complexidade.

"Toda a documentação coletada durante a inspeção está em análise prioritária para orientar a adoção das medidas administrativas cabíveis, conforme a legislação vigente", dizem os órgãos.

Segundo a Secretaria da Segurança Pública (SSP), seis casos estão sob investigação no 8º Distrito Policial do bairro.

As crianças de zero a três anos teriam contraído infecções hospitalares e morrido em decorrência de sepse (antigamente conhecida como infecção generalizada) e outras complicações.

A assistente jurídica Eduarda Fragnan Gomes, que representa três mães, diz que há pelo menos 19 casos de famílias que perderam seus filhos em cirurgias realizadas no Hospital Salvalus nos últimos seis meses.

O Hospital Salvalus pertence à rede Hapvida, do grupo NotreDame Intermédica, e fica na Rua Bresser, na Mooca, Zona Leste de SP.. — Foto: Reprodução/TV Globo

Segundo ela, boletins de ocorrência foram registrados em municípios como Praia Grande, Itaquaquecetuba, além de outras delegacias da capital paulista, como na Vila Maria.

“Muitos casos ainda não foram registrados e outros ainda não foram remetidos ao 8° DP, que centraliza as investigações. São crianças que deram entrada para fazer cirurgias de má formação, digestivas ou de correção que tinham chance baixíssima de morte, mas que tiveram infecção generalizada e faleceram. As famílias estão desoladas”, afirmou Eduarda Fragnan.

Por meio de nota, a Polícia Civil, diz que “a autoridade policial realiza diligências, inclusive com as oitivas de profissionais de saúde e testemunhas, análise integral dos prontuários médicos, visando esclarecer as causas das mortes”.

Os casos ocorreram desde o começo do ano e foram comunicados nesta quarta-feira (21).

Polícia Civil de SP investiga Hospital Salvalus pertence à rede Hapvida, do grupo NotreDame Intermédica, e fica na Rua Bresser, na Mooca, Zona Leste de SP. — Foto: Reprodução/TV Globo

Por meio de nota, o Hospital Salvalus afirmou que, até o momento, “a instituição não recebeu notificação formal sobre os procedimentos mencionados e permanece à disposição das autoridades competentes para prestar os esclarecimentos necessários, preservando o sigilo médico e a privacidade dos pacientes”.

A unidade também afirmou que “a instituição trata os relatos com máxima seriedade e ressalta que situações clínicas distintas não podem ser atribuídas a uma mesma causa sem comprovação técnica”.

“A instituição trata os relatos com máxima seriedade e ressalta que situações clínicas distintas não podem ser atribuídas a uma mesma causa sem comprovação técnica. (...) Este ano, mais de mil crianças foram atendidas, com cuidados individualizados e equipes especializadas. As avaliações realizadas até o momento apontam históricos clínicos distintos, sem identificação de uma origem infecciosa comum entre os casos examinados”, disse (veja a íntegra abaixo).

Eduarda Fragnan afirma que na próxima semana várias outras famílias serão acompanhadas ao 8º DP do Brás para registrar novos boletins de ocorrência contra o hospital

"O hospital reafirma seu compromisso com a segurança dos pacientes, a qualidade da assistência e o respeito às famílias. A instituição trata os relatos com máxima seriedade e ressalta que situações clínicas distintas não podem ser atribuídas a uma mesma causa sem comprovação técnica.

Referência em maternidade de alto risco e assistência pediátrica de alta complexidade, a unidade recebe crianças com condições graves, como prematuridade extrema, malformações, síndromes genéticas e quadros infecciosos que exigem cuidados especializados.

Este ano, mais de mil crianças foram atendidas, com cuidados individualizados e equipes especializadas. As avaliações realizadas até o momento apontam históricos clínicos distintos, sem identificação de uma origem infecciosa comum entre os casos examinados.

O hospital ressalta que alegações apresentadas não podem ser generalizadas nem utilizadas para estabelecer conclusões sobre todos os atendimentos sem respaldo técnico. Afirmações sem a devida contextualização podem ampliar a angústia de famílias que já enfrentam momentos de grande vulnerabilidade.

A unidade mantém avaliações contínuas da segurança assistencial e canais de acolhimento às famílias. Até o momento, a instituição não recebeu notificação formal sobre os procedimentos mencionados e permanece à disposição das autoridades competentes para prestar os esclarecimentos necessários, preservando o sigilo médico e a privacidade dos pacientes".

articles.title: Trabalhador sofre queimaduras durante incêndio em pastelaria de MG | G1
articles.standfirst: Segundo o Corpo de Bombeiros, o homem estava trabalhando quando o incêndio atingiu o estabelecimento, na tarde desta sexta-feira (23). Ele foi levado para o Hospital Manoel Gonçalves.
articles.summary: Segundo o Corpo de Bombeiros, o homem estava trabalhando quando o incêndio atingiu o estabelecimento, na tarde desta sexta-feira (23).
articles.body:
Um homem, que não teve a idade informada, sofreu queimaduras no corpo durante um incêndio em uma pastelaria na região central de Itaúna , na tarde desta sexta-feira (23). Segundo o Serviço de Atendimento Móvel de Urgência (Samu), a vítima foi socorrida e precisou ser levada para a Sala Vermelha do Hospital Manoel Gonçalves.

O nome do estabelecimento onde ocorreu o incêndio não foi divulgado.

O Corpo de Bombeiros foi acionado para combater as chamas, que atingiram o interior do estabelecimento e provocaram intensa fumaça. Conforme as informações iniciais, a vítima trabalhava na pastelaria no momento do incêndio.

A Polícia Militar (PM) também esteve no local para atuar nas primeiras ações da ocorrência.

Ainda não há informações sobre as causas do incêndio nem sobre o estado de saúde atualizado da vítima.

Incêndio foi registrado em uma pastelaria em Itaúna — Foto: Redes Sociais/Reprodução

Ainda nesta sexta-feira (23), uma funcionária de uma padaria no Centro de Divinópolis ficou ferida durante um incêndio. Ela sofreu queimaduras de primeiro grau em um dos braços ao tentar apagar as chamas, que já haviam sido controladas pelo proprietário. A suspeita é de que o fogo tenha começado após um vazamento de gás.

articles.title: Em cuidados paliativos, Roberto Higa celebra a vida ao lado da família | G1
articles.standfirst: Fotojornalista relembra registros históricos de Campo Grande, reúne décadas de memória em seu acervo e enfrenta um novo capítulo da vida durante o tratamento contra o câncer.
articles.summary: Fotojornalista relembra registros históricos de Campo Grande, reúne décadas de memória em seu acervo e enfrenta um novo capítulo da vida durante o tratamento contra o câncer.
articles.body:
Um dos principais nomes do fotojornalismo de Mato Grosso do Sul, Roberto Higa abriu o álbum da própria vida. Em entrevista à TV Morena, ele relembrou décadas de registros históricos de Campo Grande e falou sobre o desafio mais recente: o câncer.

Na garagem da casa do fotógrafo, o carro da família divide espaço com retratos de pessoas famosas. No interior da residência, fotos e quadros ocupam as paredes e se integram à decoração, transformando o lugar em uma espécie de galeria particular.

Cada imagem ajuda a contar a história de quem estava por trás da câmera: Roberto Higa, filho de imigrantes japoneses que se tornou uma referência do fotojornalismo no estado.

Na década de 1960, ele já registrava acontecimentos importantes com os equipamentos fotográficos da época.

"Eu fui o cara que mais fotografou presidentes em visita ao estado, Médici, Geisel", conta Higa.

Depois de tantas décadas segurando uma câmera, o fotógrafo diz que o equipamento continua fazendo parte de sua rotina, apesar das limitações físicas. "Eu fotografo até hoje, apesar da mão que já não é mais aquela".

A história de Higa também se entrelaça com a de Sandra, sua esposa. O namoro começou nos pedalinhos da Universidade Estadual de Mato Grosso, atual Universidade Federal de Mato Grosso do Sul (UFMS), em Campo Grande, antes da divisão do estado.

O local marcou o início do relacionamento e serviu de cenário para as primeiras fotografias do casal. Higa conta que o primeiro registro de Sandra foi feito nos pedalinhos da universidade, onde ficava a piscina olímpica.

Do namoro ao casamento, as lembranças permanecem guardadas. O convite da cerimônia está preservado, assim como as fotografias do casamento civil, da celebração na igreja e da festa realizada na casa onde moravam.

Na década de 1980, a câmera também registrou a chegada do primeiro filho. Higa produziu um álbum de maternidade, um tipo de ensaio que, décadas depois, se popularizaria. Há, ainda, uma história que vai além das imagens: durante o parto de um dos filhos, ele cobriu o hospital com bandeiras do Operário, time para o qual torce.

Roberto Higa registrou fotos durante a entrevista para a TV Morena — Foto: TV Morena

Dos encontros na avenida aos registros da política

Higa também fotografou festas e encontros de jovens em Campo Grande. Durante muitos fins de semana, acompanhou o movimento da chamada Avenida da Paquera, na Avenida Afonso Pena, região que hoje integra o centro da cidade. Na época, o local reunia jovens e contava até com alto-falantes para facilitar os encontros amorosos.

"As moças ficavam desfilando pelo asfalto, e tinha um alto-falante em cima do relógio, em cada esquina tinha um auto falante: 'Atenção atenção, você moça que está de saia plissada, blusinha branca, maria-chiquinha no cabelo, o fulano de tal tá te esperando na rua Maracaju", relembra.

"Tiveram que parar de deixar o pessoal ficar circulando, por que se não não parava para a inauguração", relembra.ens até eventos políticos. Higa registrou as transformações do monumento, desde a estrutura original e sua retirada até as mudanças de localização e a instalação do modelo atual.

A chegada da primeira escada rolante a uma loja de departamentos do centro de Campo Grande também ficou registrada em seu acervo. Com a câmera em mãos, ele fotografou a reação das pessoas ao experimentar a novidade.

"Tiveram que parar de deixar o pessoal ficar circulando, porque se não não parava para a inauguração", relembra.

Ao longo da carreira, o fotógrafo acompanhou comícios, eventos políticos e acontecimentos que marcaram a formação do estado, entre eles a Assembleia Estadual Constituinte de 1979, responsável pela elaboração da Constituição de Mato Grosso do Sul após a divisão do antigo estado de Mato Grosso. Os registros desse período também fazem parte de seu arquivo.

Em uma das visitas do então presidente Emílio Garrastazu Médici a Campo Grande, um dia de chuva ficou marcado na memória do fotógrafo.

"Cheguei a fotografar o Médici fumando, o que não acontecia para todo mundo, porque o presidente não podia entrar fumando, e ele gostava de fumar", conta.

Na época, Higa tinha um crachá que facilitava o acesso às coberturas de presidentes e candidatos à Presidência da República. Muitos de seus cartões profissionais estão reunidos em um quadro na residência.

A trajetória da Rede Matogrossense de Comunicação (RMC), do grupo de comunicação e da família Zahran também está documentada na casa. Sandra é responsável por organizar e preservar parte desse material.

Segundo ela, as imagens estão catalogadas em cadernos e envelopes, cada um com os respectivos negativos. Ao todo, são mais de 8.700 envelopes registrados em um caderno.

O acervo da vida e o desafio do tratamento

Neste ano, a trajetória de Higa também virou documentário e filme. Mas, enquanto sua história profissional ganha novos registros, o fotógrafo enfrenta um dos capítulos mais difíceis da vida.

Diagnosticado com câncer na laringe, ele passou por tratamento em Campo Grande, em um hospital que acompanhou desde a fundação. Ao longo dessa jornada, ele e a família registraram diferentes etapas do processo. Ao concluir um dos ciclos de tratamento, Higa tocou o sino no Hospital Alfredo Abrão, gesto que simboliza o encerramento de uma etapa.

Meses depois, um vídeo gravado no sofá de casa trouxe a notícia da volta da doença. Atualmente, o fotógrafo recebe cuidados paliativos e conta com o apoio da família.

Ao ser perguntado se tem noção de tudo o que já fez ao longo da vida, Higa responde: "Eu tenho, e me dou por satisfeito", finaliza.

Roberto Higa relembrou histórias durante entrevista à TV Morena. — Foto: TV Morena

articles.title: Sem saber que estava grávida, mulher dá à luz em banheiro no RN | G1
articles.standfirst: Paciente buscou atendimento após se queixar de dores abdominais e deu à luz no hospital municipal de Grossos, no Oeste potiguar, na madrugada de quinta-feira (22).
articles.summary: Após procurar atendimento por dores abdominais em Grossos, paciente deu à luz no banheiro do hospital sem saber que estava grávida.
articles.body:
Mulher iniciou trabalho de parto enquanto estava em banheiro de hospital — Foto: Reprodução

Uma mulher deu à luz dentro do banheiro do Hospital Municipal Flaviana Jacinta, em Grossos, na região Oeste do Rio Grande do Norte, na madrugada de quinta-feira (22). Ela havia procurado atendimento por causa de dores abdominais e, até aquele momento, não sabia que estava grávida, segundo a própria paciente.

Segundo informações da Prefeitura de Grossos, a mulher começou a sentir dores na noite de quarta-feira (21) e pediu uma ambulância para chegar à unidade de saúde. Ao ir ao banheiro do hospital, ela sentiu dores mais fortes e gritou por ajuda. A equipe médica constatou que ela estava em trabalho de parto.

O médico Osmar Filho, que atendeu a paciente, contou que a equipe ouviu os gritos e foi até o banheiro. Em seguida, a mulher foi levada para a sala de estabilização, onde recebeu atendimento durante o parto.

“Graças a Deus a criança nasceu bem, sem intercorrências. A mãe todo tempo esteve estável hemodinamicamente”, relatou o médico.

Após o nascimento, a equipe entrou em contato com o Hospital da Mulher, referência para o atendimento, e transferiu a mãe e a bebê para avaliação das equipes de pediatria e obstetrícia.

"Fizemos a transferência da paciente para poder ser avaliada tanto pela equipe da pediatria quanto pela equipe de obstetras", acresentou o profissional.

articles.title: Americana: motorista fica ferido ao bater carro contra muro de viaduto | G1
articles.standfirst: Homem de 42 anos foi socorrido e levado ao Hospital Municipal Doutor Waldemar Tebaldi após o acidente na manhã desta sexta-feira (23).
articles.summary: Homem de 42 anos foi socorrido e levado ao Hospital Municipal Doutor Waldemar Tebaldi após o acidente na manhã desta sexta-feira (23).
articles.body:
Motorista fica ferido após bater carro contra muro de viaduto em Americana — Foto: Guarda Municipal de Americana/Divulgação

Um motorista de 42 anos ficou ferido após bater o carro que dirigia contra o muro lateral do Viaduto Ministro Ralph Biasi , na região central de Americana (SP), na manhã desta sexta-feira (23).

Segundo a Guarda Municipal, o homem conduzia um veículo com placas de Santa Bárbara d’Oeste (SP), e trafegava no sentido da Avenida da Saudade. Ao entrar no viaduto, ele colidiu contra a estrutura .

Durante o atendimento da ocorrência, o motorista relatou aos guardas que não se lembrava das circunstâncias exatas que provocaram o acidente.

Ele não soube informar se teve a passagem fechada por outro veículo ou se perdeu o controle da direção. O airbag foi acionado e o homem relatou dores na região do peito abdômen.

Depois de receber os primeiros atendimentos no local, foi encaminhado ao Hospital Municipal Doutor Waldemar Tebaldi para avaliação e cuidados médicos.

A Guarda Municipal permaneceu no trecho do acidente para orientar os motoristas e sinalizar o trânsito na via.

articles.title: First personalised cancer vaccine cuts risk of disease returning in major trial
articles.summary: The scientists involved say the results could mark a turning point in cancer treatment, bringing personalised medicine a step closer.
articles.body:
A new personalised cancer vaccine given alongside a widely used immunotherapy drug has cut the risk of patients dying or their skin cancer returning by 42% in a major clinical trial.

The researchers involved say the results could mark a turning point in cancer treatment, bringing personalised medicine a step closer.

The trial also found that the new drug combination reduced the risk of melanoma, a type of skin cancer, spreading by 38% over two years compared to immunotherapy alone.

The drug manufacturers MSD and Moderna say the same approach is already being tested against other tumours, including kidney, bladder and lung cancer.

Independent cancer experts described the results as impressive but said longer-term studies were still needed to establish whether the treatment really helps most patients live longer, on average.

The new approach is aimed at cancer patients who have already had their tumour removed through surgery.

In the trial, 1,137 adults were given Keytruda, an established immunotherapy drug which helps the body's immune system find and attack cancer cells.

About two-thirds also received an experimental vaccine with the rest being given a placebo or dummy drug.

The vaccine, called Intismeran, uses the same mRNA technology as some Covid jabs.

It is personalised to each patient, using information from their own tumour to help train their immune system to recognise cancer cells and target them if they return.

Two years after starting the treatment, the patients who received the jab were far less likely to have had melanoma come back or see it spread across the body.

"Personalisation is the next step up and it's really exciting, it's a fabulous technology," says Prof Pippa Corrie, a consultant medical oncologist who helped run part of the study with patients at Addenbrooke's Hospital in Cambridge.

"The question is how much can we really demonstrate it's worth and this trial was the first proof of principle."

Prof Corrie worked with patients enrolled in the trial including 75-year old Tony Chapman, who was diagnosed with melanoma in 2019.

He had the tumour removed from his chest but a lump later appeared under his arm. He was told his cancer had returned and he needed a second operation.

He then volunteered to take part in the study but, like all the other participants, he still doesn't know whether he was given the experimental vaccine or a placebo alongside his immunotherapy treatment.

"This just seemed like a really good example of moving science forward, as well as getting some benefit for yourself, so what's to lose?" Tony said.

Three years on he is now having checks every six months and remains cancer-free.

Shares in the drugmakers MSD (known as Merck in the US) and Moderna have surged since both companies first hinted at the success of the vaccine in the summer.

But investors sold off stock on Thursday after financial analysts said the results were not quite as strong as those seen in an earlier, much smaller trial.

Both companies said they were now "engaging with authorities" suggesting they could file for approval from medicine regulators as soon as next year.

Widespread NHS use will also depend on cost, given that each individual patient will need to have their tumour genetically analysed and a personalised vaccine made for them.

The trial will continue so that the patients involved can be monitored – both to see if the cancer returns over time and to assess whether the drug ultimately helps them live longer.

Professor Alan Melcher from the Institute of Cancer Research in London, who wasn't involved in the research, described the results as "very impressive".

"It is an important proof of principle for the field, although we shouldn't get ahead of the evidence," he said.

"We can't assume from one melanoma trial that the same approach will work across all cancers, and longer follow-up will be important to understand the effect on overall survival."

The full trial results are due to be presented at the European Society of Medical Oncology (ESMO) cancer conference in Madrid on Saturday.

They have yet to be published in a peer-reviewed medical journal, where they can be scrutinised by independent experts.

articles.title: Second autopsy after woman lawyer’s death in locked flat raises family’s doubts
articles.summary: Second autopsy held after Hazaribag lawyer Anushka Chakraborty found hanging in locked flat; family disputes suicide, alleges harassment; police probe code lock.
articles.body: Hazaribag: A second post-mortem examination was conducted on Friday on the body of 28-year-old Anushka Chakraborty, a day after the lawyer was found hanging inside the room of her apartment in Hazaribag’s Bengali Colony, as her family refused to accept the death as a suicide and demanded a deeper probe.Anushka’s body was found around 10 am on Thursday in the apartment, which falls under Bada Bazar police station limits. Police have seized electronic devices and are examining the sequence of events before her death, including how and when the flat’s electronic code lock was activated.Her brother, Devjit Chakraborty, has raised questions over a message reportedly sent to their mother before the death. He said Anushka usually communicated with her mother through calls or voice notes and, whenever she texted, wrote in Bengali. The final message, however, was typed in Hindi.The message reportedly said: “Mom, please forgive me, but I cannot bear this anymore. I know I cannot come back home. My husband himself told me that only my corpse will leave from here, so this is for the best. I will not be able to live. I am completely exhausted now. I just can’t do this anymore. Sorry, Mom.”Devjit alleged that Anushka had suffered a miscarriage days earlier and was later taunted and mentally harassed by her husband, Kushagra Rudra, and her in-laws over her inability to bear a child. Police have not independently established the allegations, which remain under investigation.The family has also pointed to photographs and videos from Sindoor Khela celebrations on Wednesday, saying Anushka appeared happy hours before her death.Bada Bazar police station officer in-charge Mukesh Kumar Rajak said police were looking for Rudra, who had not returned to Hazaribag even 24 hours after the incident. Police said Rudra called emergency number 100 but did not come to the apartment. When contacted, he reportedly said he was in Palamu and would return soon.Police entered the flat with help from Rudra’s driver. Investigators are now trying to determine who locked the apartment and when. Anushka’s parents have demanded justice. Ramgarh MLA Mamta Devi met the family at Sadar Hospital.Stay updated with the latest Ranchi news. Download the TOI App.

articles.title: Jersey's health spending on Southampton taxis surges by 75%
articles.summary: It comes as the department looks to review spending for off-island hospital treatment.
articles.body:
The amount of money spent on taxis for Jersey patients visiting Southampton hospital and the surrounding area has risen by 75% in two years.

In 2023, £140,594 was spent on taxi provision, which surged to £246,542 in 2025.

Islanders can request a taxi if it is "not possible or practical" to use public transport, or if there is a "medical reason" to do so.

The Health department has been asked for comment.

The government's patient travel policy states that travel from a port to a UK hospital should be on services contracted by Health and Care Jersey.

Were that was not possible, "patients should use public transport and pay for this themselves" and have the costs reimbursed by the Travel Office.

It also said that where there was a "medical reason", or it was not "possible or practical" to use other means, "the Travel Office could consider and, if necessary, pre-book a taxi or hire car as appropriate".

In a Freedom Of Information (FOI) request , Health & Care Jersey published the amount of money spent on taxis over the last three years.

It showed that spending has risen by just over 75% since 2023:

Health and Care Jersey said the figures cover travel in areas around Southampton and "cannot be considered representative of expenditure on taxis for patients attending Southampton hospital alone".

It comes as patient travel costs are being reviewed, after being described as "very generous" by a Health Board leader.

Following that intervention, Health Minister Tom Binet said he would consider whether "UK travel should continue to be paid for all patients in all circumstances".

He said: "The health budget is under growing pressure...[and] it is essential that all our resources are used in the most effective way".

"Officers are actively working to ensure that the costs we currently pay...represent value for money".

The health department has been approached for further comment.

articles.title: Man, 100, and Wife, 99, Share 6 Tips for a Long Life and Their ‘Secret Weapon’ for Longevity
articles.summary: 100-year-old Bernie Gerson and his wife Eleanor have been married 80 years. They share their longevity tips, crediting this breakfast food and healthy habits.
articles.body: Eleanor and Bernie Gerson marked their 80th wedding anniversary this year, but there’s so much more to celebrate. He’ll be 101 years old in November; she’ll turn 100 in January. They met as teenagers but went their separate ways until “destiny” brought them back together, he says. The couple lives independently with the help of their daughter who resides with them in Warrington, Pennsylvania. “We are very, very thankful for still being together,” Bernie Gerson tells TODAY.com. His wife is still amazed by their whirlwind marriage, which came after he proposed via letter while serving on a U.S. Navy warship in the Pacific during World War II. “Now I look back at it, I realize how young we really were, and how much we have had to find out about life,” Eleanor Gerson says. He drove a car and played tennis until his 90s, and has a “secret weapon” when it comes to his diet. She always liked to be active, walking, volunteering and helping others. “I feel that having each other has kept them going this long,” their granddaughter, Allison Snyder, tells TODAY.com. She likes to describe her grandparents as “peanut butter and jelly” because they’re inseparable. Their daughter, Renee Gerson, 79, believes healthy eating, exercise and always being involved in the community have been important factors. Here are the couple’s simple tips for a long life: Eat a Healthy Diet Both credit wheat germ, which they’ve been eating for as long as they can remember, for their longevity, Snyder says. Bernie Gerson sprinkles a heaping tablespoon of wheat germ on his cereal every morning, calling it his “secret weapon” for good health and smooth skin. “Nobody takes me for my age because I don’t look like a lot of people who are 101,” he says. Wheat germ is the “healthiest part of the wheat kernel,” according to the University of California, Davis. It’s a “unique source of concentrated nutrients,” researchers note, and is rich in bioactive components with antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties, studies have found. It’s also a good source of “anti‐aging polyamines,” compounds that can play a role in preventing chronic diseases. Bernie Gerson’s daily morning meal of cereal with wheat germ and milk also includes crushed walnuts, sliced almonds, blueberries, strawberries and a banana. Eleanor Gerson eats oatmeal with blueberries, honey and cinnamon for breakfast. She also likes berries and apples, which are among the healthiest fruits. Both love cinnamon buns and pastries with their coffee, but keep the portions small. The couple usually skips lunch and has a variety of foods for dinner, including eggplant parmesan, fish, grilled cheese, pasta or eggs. They don’t drink alcohol. Stay at a Healthy Weight The Gersons made an effort to avoid weight creep, or the tendency to gain weight as people age. It can lead to obesity and increase the risk of heart disease and other chronic illnesses, studies have found. “I always watched my weight through the years, and my wife does, too,” Bernie Gerson says. “We’ve never been heavy in our whole life.” He loves chocolate, for example, but holds himself back — enjoying just a little taste. The centenarian still wears the same size suit he wore when he was a young adult. Be Active Eleanor Gerson introduced her husband to tennis by signing them both up for lessons and “created a monster,” she jokes. He was reluctant to go at first, but got hooked on it immediately and played until he was 94. Some doctors believe tennis is the healthiest sport because it’s a whole-body workout. Bernie Gerson also played basketball, football and baseball, and took up jogging when few other people were running. “Being healthy and in shape was a very important thing in my life,” he says. Eleanor Gerson shared that goal. “I always liked to be active. I enjoyed that, and I think that makes a happy person,” she notes. She regularly walked and played tennis for a while. Laugh and Talk “We like to laugh a lot, Ellie and I. I think that keeps you young and keeps your mind in good shape,” Bernie Gerson says. His granddaughter calls him a “naturally happy person” who likes to tell jokes. Her grandmother is the conversationalist. The couple enjoys discussing current events and politics at dinner together every evening, Snyder notes. Bernie Gerson’s No. 1 rule for couples is to never go to bed mad. “You should stay up all night and fight,” he says. “Always have respect for one another and admire your spouse.” Love Deeply The Pennsylvania couple met in 1941 when both their families were vacationing in Atlantic City and stayed next door to each other. He was not quite 16, she was 14. “I used to see her go to the beach, and I’d say, ‘She’s so pretty, I would love to meet her,’” Bernie Gerson recalls. They did meet on the boardwalk when he asked a mutual friend to introduce them. He jotted down her phone number, but they didn’t stay in touch when she went back to Philadelphia and he to Norristown. About two years later, Bernie Gerson was on a date with another girl in Philadelphia when he spotted Eleanor with her date at a dance. He called her the next day. Bumping into her again was “destiny,” the centenarian believes. Bernie Gerson proposed marriage in a letter while serving in the U.S. Navy on board the USS Wilkes-Barre during World War II. The Purple Heart recipient was at sea in the Pacific Ocean, so it took months for him to find out she accepted. When he came home, she told him, “You’re under no obligation. We don’t really know each other that well.” But she was willing to go with it, she says. “We’re getting married,” he replied. The wedding took place nine weeks later on July 14, 1946. Stay Positive Bernie Gerson says his father told him at an early age that he should have “good MA,” or mental attitude. “He’s so right. If you think positive, it’s a wonderful gift,” Gerson says. “It’s easy to be negative and talk bad about things, but if you have a good MA, you can almost overcome anything that happens to you.”

articles.title: Craig Melvin Jokes This 1 Trendy Workout Helped Him Nab People’s Sexiest Morning Show Host
articles.summary: Craig Melvin reveals the workout that helped him win the morning host category in People’s Sexiest Man Alive Readers’ Choice poll and the benefits of Pilates.
articles.body: Craig Melvin didn’t reach “Sexiest Man Alive” status just by sitting on the couch — he had help from a famous workout. The TODAY co-anchor recently won the “hotter than your cup of coffee” morning host category in the People’s Sexiest Man Alive Readers’ Choice poll. It may have helped that Savannah Guthrie encouraged viewers to “vote early and often” after he was nominated last month. But guests on the show also couldn’t resist asking Craig about how he accomplished the feat and stays in shape. “Tell us what you did, I think people want to know,” NBC News medical contributor Dr. Akshay Syal teasingly inquired during a segment about exercise goals for every age on Friday, Oct. 23. The inquiry prompted laughter from TODAY’s Dylan Dreyer and Laura Jarrett. “Pilates — a lot of Pilates, because I was having issues with my back and my core,” Craig answered. “You too can win the award if you do Pilates,” Syal jokingly told the viewers. Pilates, named after founder Joseph Pilates, focuses on exercises to strengthen and tone the core — which includes the abs, back, hips and glutes — plus the arms and legs, explains TODAY Fitness contributor Stephanie Mansour, a certified personal trainer and a yoga and Pilates instructor. Repeated movements work the midsection, which can be especially beneficial for people with back problems, she adds. The low-impact workout helped to cure her chronic back pain. Pilates can be done on a mat or a reformer machine. When Craig previously tried the machine version, he called it “perhaps the most intense” workout he’d ever done, noting that it left him sore for three days afterward. Mansour recommends these 20 simple Pilates exercises for beginners to strengthen the core, relieve back pain and flatten the stomach.

articles.title: Chhawla tank victims entered confined space without protective gear: cops
articles.summary: Delhi Chhawla septic/water tank death: Police say 4 men entered confined space without safety gear; 1 dead, 3 hospitalised; negligence case filed.
articles.body: New Delhi: Delhi Police, probing the death of a man at an under-construction septic/water tank in southwest Delhi’s Chhawla on Oct 21, have found that he and three others, who fell sick after inhaling toxic fumes, had entered the tank without wearing protective safety gear.A preliminary inquiry revealed that the incident occurred inside an under-construction water/septic tank on a residential plot. Police said the tank did not contain sewage or water at the time. The four men had allegedly entered the confined space to remove shuttering and inspect construction work when they inhaled toxic gases.According to investigators, a contractor, identified as Madan Pandit (38), entered the tank after labourer Vinod (22) climbed inside and stopped responding. Pandit went down to check on him. When neither of the two emerged, the plot owner’s sons, Chander Shekhar (35) and Surender Singh (42), allegedly entered the tank in an attempt to rescue them but fell sick after inhaling toxic fumes. Pandit was taken to a hospital, where he was declared dead on arrival. The three others are undergoing treatment, said police.Police said a mobile crime team inspected the spot and photographed the scene. Pandit’s body was shifted to the mortuary at RTRM Hospital for post-mortem and other legal formalities.A case of negligence has been registered, and police are investigating whether the construction work had the necessary permissions and whether any safety lapses contributed to the incident. No arrests have been made so far.The incident is the latest in a series of deaths linked to toxic gases in confined spaces in Delhi. In June this year, three men died after inhaling toxic fumes inside a septic tank at a factory in Mundka Industrial Area. In May 2025, a man died after entering a septic tank at a house in New Ashok Nagar, while another person was injured during a rescue attempt. articles.title: NHRC seeks cop action on plaint over Hailakandi schoolgirl gang rape-murder within 8 weeks
articles.summary: NHRC directs Hailakandi police to act in 8 weeks on complaint over alleged gang rape-murder of 15-year-old; JJB recommends 16-year-old be tried as adult.
articles.body: Silchar: The National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) has directed Hailakandi police to act within eight weeks on a complaint over the alleged gang rape and murder of a 15-year-old schoolgirl.The directive followed a complaint filed by Delhi-based social activist Krishna Rajput through HRCNet portal on Sept 2. The complaint sought a fair, time-bound investigation and accountability for any lapses by public authorities.According to NHRC’s action-taken record dated Oct 19, the complaint was disposed of with directions and forwarded to the Hailakandi SP for appropriate action within eight weeks. The police have also been asked to inform the complainant of the action taken.The complaint raised concerns over alleged violations of the victim’s right to life, dignity and bodily integrity, and sought the preservation of medical and forensic evidence. It also called for an examination of possible negligence or dereliction of duty by public officials and action against those found responsible.NHRC’s directive comes amid developments in the criminal proceedings. Juvenile Justice Board (JJB) in Hailakandi has recommended that a 16-year-old accused be considered for trial as an adult following a preliminary assessment under the Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act.The order was passed by the board’s principal magistrate after considering the alleged offence, psychological assessment reports from Silchar Medical College and Hospital, and a report submitted by the investigating officer.Under the Juvenile Justice Act, children aged 16 to 18 accused of heinous offences may undergo a preliminary assessment to determine whether they should face trial as adults. The final decision rests with the Children’s Court, which will examine the matter independently. The assessment does not establish the juvenile’s guilt.The special investigation team (SIT) earlier filed a chargesheet against five accused, including four adults and the juvenile. The investigation involved forensic evidence, medico-legal reports, digital records, witness statements and seized materials.The chargesheet was filed under Section 193 of the BNSS. The case was initially registered under Sections 65(1) and 103(1) of the BNS, read with Section 6 of the Pocso Act. Police later invoked additional provisions of the BNS.According to police, the schoolgirl was found in a bloodied condition inside her residence on the night of Aug 1 while her family members were attending a social event. Police began investigating after receiving information about the incident, and forensic experts collected evidence from the scene.Five accused were arrested in connection with the case. The juvenile’s identity has been withheld in accordance with the law.The incident triggered protests across Hailakandi district, with residents, women’s organisations and civil society groups demanding stringent punishment and speedy justice for the victim’s family.The NHRC complaint is separate from the criminal proceedings and concerns accountability for the authorities’ handling of the case.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Guwahati | Silver Rate in Guwahati | Bank Holidays in Guwahati | Public Holidays in Guwahati | Guwahati AQI | Weather in Guwahati | Petrol Price in Guwahati | Diesel Price in Guwahati | CNG Price in Guwahati | LPG Price in GuwahatiStay updated with the latest Guwahati news. articles.title: Student killed in wall collapse due to heavy rain;  southern TN braces for more
articles.summary: Heavy rains in southern Tamil Nadu kill 17-year-old in Virudhunagar, damage homes, disrupt Kodaikanal traffic; red alert issued for hill districts.
articles.body: Madurai: Heavy rains across southern Tamil Nadu left a Class XII student dead in Sattur in Virudhunagar district, damaged several houses, temporarily cut off roads to Kodaikanal and caused check dams to overflow on Friday. Flooding also forced restrictions at popular waterfalls, while rising reservoir levels prompted warnings to riverside communities.S Muthuselvi, 17, died after a wall collapsed inside her family’s tiled-roof house at Mettamalai near Sattur in Virudhunagar district around 11pm Thursday. The family was asleep when the central wall gave way following hours of rain. Her mother, Solaiammal, suffered a leg fracture. Neighbours pulled them from the debris and took them to Sattur govt hospital, where the girl died on Friday morning.The student attended Government Higher Secondary School in Chinnakamanpatti. Her father, Selvam, a daily wage worker, escaped injury. Social welfare minister K Jegadeshwari visited the hospital on Friday, handed the family Rs4 lakh in govt relief and assured assistance to construct a new house. Police registered a case.In M Vellalapatti near Melur, roofs of five houses collapsed and four others were partly damaged, but residents escaped injury after vacating the buildings. Elsewhere, an 85-year-old woman was injured by a falling wall in Thoothukudi, three houses were damaged near Kayathar, and a farmer’s house was destroyed at Kovilankulam in Ramanathapuram district.Meanwhile, floodwater near Shenbaganur disrupted access to Kodaikanal, leaving tourist cars and buses stranded for nearly two hours on Friday. Dindigul collector advised tourists against travelling to Kodaikanal due to landslides, fallen trees and flooding along access roads. Tourists were also barred from bathing at Kumbakkarai in Theni, Thiruparappu in Kanniyakumari and major Courtallam waterfalls in Tenkasi, where swollen streams made entry unsafe.In Theni, where Thekkady recorded 7.5cm of rain, the Anaipillaiyar check dam near Bodi overflowed, while Sothuparai reservoir reached its full level of 126.28 feet, releasing excess water into the Varaha river. Vaigai and Mullaperiyar reservoirs rose to 46.52 feet and 119.75 feet, respectively, prompting authorities to warn people against entering swollen rivers or crossing flooded stretches.The weather department issued a red alert for extremely heavy rain in the hill areas of Tirunelveli and Kanyakumari on Friday. Very heavy rain is forecast there and in Theni on Saturday, with Madurai and neighbouring districts facing further downpours on Sunday. articles.title: Personalized mRNA vaccine for melanoma cut risk of cancer’s return in late-stage trial
articles.summary: Moderna and Merck’s personalized mRNA vaccine for melanoma reduced the risk of cancer recurrence and death by 42% compared with standard treatment in a trial.
articles.body: A new personalized mRNA vaccine for melanoma is being hailed by some oncologists as a major breakthrough after it reduced the risk of cancer recurrence and death by 42% compared with standard treatment in a late-stage clinical trial. Dr. Robert Vonderheide, director of Penn Medicine’s Abramson Cancer Center and president-elect of the American Association for Cancer Research, said the results are a “game changer.” “It will be seen as the first step toward using cancer vaccines to their full potential,” said Vonderheide, who was not involved in the trial. The experimental vaccine, called intismeran, was developed by drugmakers Moderna and Merck. Intismeran is personalized to each patient, using genomic data from the patient’s tumor. The new results will be presented Saturday at the annual meeting of the European Society for Medical Oncology in Madrid. The trial included 1,137 Stage 3 melanoma patients. All of the participants had undergone surgery to remove their tumors and were being treated with Merck’s immunotherapy drug Keytruda. In addition to Keytruda, 757 of the participants also got the personalized vaccine; the remaining 380 got a placebo. Two years later, 82% of the patients who received both the new vaccine and the immunotherapy hadn’t had a recurrence, compared with 70% in the immunotherapy plus placebo group. In Stage 3 melanoma, the cancer has spread to nearby lymph nodes or other sites on the skin, but it hasn’t spread to distant organs. Cancer recurrence is the “dreaded event” for these patients, Vonderheide said. If it does return, spread to distant organs is more likely. Dr. Georgina Long, co-medical director of the Melanoma Institute Australia who led the clinical trial, said that while scans might suggest that melanoma has been completely removed by surgery, invisible cancer cells may still be lurking. “This treatment is about mopping up the cancer cells we can’t see,” Long said. “We know with [Keytruda] alone, that works really well, but not in everyone.” Keytruda works by mobilizing immune cells called T cells to spot and destroy cancer. The vaccine also helps the immune system fight cancer. Each vaccine is created by taking the excised tumor, sequencing its genome and identifying a tell-tale fingerprint of abnormal proteins known as neoantigens, Long said. The vaccine trains the immune system to recognize and target these neoantigens, similar to how a standard vaccine is trained to recognize and target a virus or bacteria. Intismeran uses messenger RNA technology, the same platform pioneered in the development of Covid vaccines that’s hailed for how quickly it can be rolled out. Each patient received their personalized vaccine in a little over nine weeks on average. “They’re not on the shelf,” Vonderheide said. “They have to be made for that patient. Can that be done in a few weeks in order to have a timely treatment? Turns out, the answer to that is yes.” Dr. Shirin Bajaj, incoming director of hHead and nNeck mMelanoma at Mount Sinai in New York, said that while Keytruda works by taking the brakes off the immune system and enabling it to recognize cancer cells, the new vaccine is likely enhancing its abilities by mobilizing additional immune cells called killer T cells. “It essentially creates an army of killer T cells that are meant to recognize the tumor,” said Bajaj, who was not involved in the trial. Side effects of the vaccine included pain around the injection site and a mild fever — similar to those seen with Covid vaccines. For Dr. Gino In, an associate professor at the USC Keck School of Medicine Norris Comprehensive Cancer Center in Los Angeles, that is a major selling point. In some cases, Keytruda can result in serious organ inflammation, and previous attempts to combine the immunotherapies with other drugs have not only failed to improve cancer recurrence outcomes, but resulted in worse side effects. “In prior trials, other drugs that were studied in combination with [this class of immunotherapies] led to significant, and eventually potentially permanent side effects, particularly side effects that triggered the immune system to attack our own body,” In, who wasn’t involved with the trial, wrote in an email. Despite the positive results, investors reacted poorly when the findings were leaked on Thursday, causing Moderna’s stock price to fall. Bajaj said that this may be because while the trial’s results are a significant breakthrough for the field of cancer vaccines, the difference between taking Keytruda and the vaccine compared with Keytruda alone is still relatively modest. “The reality is that on one hand, any difference you see is amazing because it’s one more option for a patient,” she said. “Is this likely helpful for a handful of patients? I would say yes, but it’s hard to say whether at this point we have data to suggest that this is actually the next blockbuster.” The full data is yet to be published in a peer-reviewed journal, and Bajaj said that the patients in the trial still need to be followed for several more years to see whether the vaccine continues to offer additional benefits in terms of preventing the return and spread of melanoma as well as its effects on survival. In addition, Bajaj said she had questions over the scalability of the treatment. She noted that of the 1,749 melanoma patients who were initially screened for participation in the trial, 17% did not have tumor samples that were big enough for a vaccine to be created. “It’s amazing, but I think some of the logistics are going to need to be worked out,” she said. “But nothing that I saw from this study made me think that the logistics are infeasible. It’s just that it will be a hurdle to actually do this at a wide scale.” However, Vonderheide described the results as a very welcome boost for the field of cancer vaccines. In recent months, the German company BioNTech announced clinical trial failures for experimental vaccines for colorectal and head and neck cancers. He suggested that intismeran’s success may be because the Merck and Moderna trial focused on preventing melanoma recurrence rather than prolonging survival in later stage patients. “The field of cancer vaccines has been filled with disappointments in treating patients with advanced disease,” Vonderheide said. “Some people look at those results and say, ‘cancer vaccines will never work.’ These results show that cancer vaccines are incredibly powerful when deployed in the right clinical setting. Vaccines work to prevent.” Still, intismeran is being studied in a separate clinical trial in patients with advanced melanoma that has already spread to distant organs. “This is just the proof of concept,” Long said. “We’re going into advanced melanoma, but we’re also doing work in many other cancers — bladder cancer, kidney cancer, lung cancer, using this concept.” She said that researchers will also be actively working to understand more about why the vaccine worked to see if that can lead to further clues. Vonderheide described the future possibilities for preventing cancer recurrence as being myriad. “One day, we might be able to think of how to use a cancer vaccine to prevent cancer in the first place,” he said. “That’s a very ambitious, far-off goal. But these results bring that goal even closer to reality than we might think.”

articles.title: Flu Activity is Ramping Up Early This Year. Is a Mutated H1N1 Strain to Blame?
articles.summary: The 2026-2027 flu season is starting early, fueled by an H1N1 strain with a new mutation. Here’s where flu activity is surging and how to protect yourself.
articles.body: If you’re surprised to hear about people getting sick with the flu before Halloween, you’re not alone. The 2026-2027 flu season appears to be off to an early and strong start, experts say. Influenza activity is still low nationally, but cases are rising quickly in many parts of the country, especially the West, and two states, Louisiana and Hawaii, are already reporting moderate levels. As of Oct. 21, flu infections are growing or likely growing in 44 states, according to the latest estimates from the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. That’s not surprising, given that flu activity typically ticks up around this time of year. However, this year’s flu season started way ahead of schedule, with infections rising as early as August. “Early-season influenza activity is currently higher than typically observed at this time of year,” the CDC said in its FluView surveillance report for the week ending Oct. 17. Influenza A H1N1 is fueling the vast majority of cases in the U.S. so far this season, per CDC data. That’s a shift from last winter, when H3N2 subclade K — aka, the “superflu” — was the dominant strain. What’s more, it appears that the H1N1 strain circulating has picked up a new mutation which may affect its ability to evade pre-existing immunity. If H1N1 sounds familiar, that’s because it’s the infamous “swine flu” strain that caused a pandemic in 2009. As the mutated H1N1 strain spreads, doctors are urging people to get the 2026-2027 flu vaccine. Why Is Flu Season Starting So Early? No two flu seasons look the same because the timing and severity can vary from year to year. However, there are multiple indicators that flu activity is higher than usual for this time of year. Cases started increasing in late August and early September and have been rising steadily since, per the CDC. The percent of flu tests coming back positive was 5.7% during the week ending Oct. 17. Last year during the same time period, the weekly test positivity rate was less than 1%, per the CDC National Respiratory and Enteric Virus Surveillance System dashboard. Outpatient visits to doctor’s offices or urgent cares for flu-like illness hit 2.2% during the week ending Oct. 17, which is higher than the previous two seasons, CDC data show. Hospitalizations and deaths from the flu are also rising. “Cases are still relatively low, so we’re still in the early phases of a flu surge,” Andrew Pekosz, Ph.D., a virologist at the Johns Hopkins Bloomberg School of Public Health, tells TODAY.com. It’s unclear why exactly cases are rising earlier than normal. One potential reason is that people may have less pre-existing immunity to the H1N1 strain with a new mutation. “Maybe that’s why people are getting sick sooner,” Dr. Bernard Camins, an infectious disease physician and professor at the Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai, tells TODAY.com. The H1N1 strain spreading is different from the H3N2 strain that dominated last winter. “Even people who got the flu last year are vulnerable,” says Camins. When H1N1 started ramping up in late August, the updated flu shots had just started rolling out. “The pattern we oftentimes see with early season flu is that the first strain that gets here is the one that escapes immunity the most,” Pekosz adds. Does an early flu season mean a more severe flu season? Not necessarily, experts say. It’s too early to tell how the 2026-2027 flu season will pan out, or whether it’ll be milder compared to last year’s. The U.S. saw a harsh flu season last winter fueled by the highly mutated H3N2 subclade K variant, aka the “super flu.” “We still have to see how bad it will be this year, but I think it is just starting earlier,” says Camins. “The only thing predictable about the flu is that it’s unpredictable,” Dr. Natalie Azar, NBC News medical contributor, said on TODAY. What Is the Mutated H1N1 Strain? Influenza viruses mutate constantly, which is why we get an updated flu shot every year. Last summer, H3N2 picked up a host of mutations, which led to the emergence the subclade K variant. H1N1 viruses typically change less often than H3N2 viruses, the CDC says. However, this year, H1N1 (pdm09), subclade D.3.1.1, acquired one new mutation, G155E, says Pekosz. The mutation was first identified in September in Seattle, Washington, according in a preprint paper published to bioRxiv. “It is different from last year’s H1N1 virus, and that mutation position (G155E) we know is important for generating protective antibody responses,” Pekosz explains. This means the H1N1 strain may be better able to escape immunity because the antibodies people have from previous infection or vaccination may not recognize it as well. “How that (mutation) is going to affect the disease spread and severity is not clear,” says Pekosz. Even if the H1N1 strain circulating does not match the one included in the 2026-2027 flu vaccines, the shot is still expected to provide protection. “A mismatch is not a black-or-white situation. We may have less immunity, not no immunity,” Pekosz adds. Historically, H1N1 has hit young people particularly hard. The new mutation may make children more susceptible, especially if they haven’t been exposed to H1N1 yet, Azar said. “It is too early to know what viruses may predominate or to say whether there might be implications on flu vaccine effectiveness this season,” the CDC said in its latest FluView report. H1N1 Flu Symptoms The flu often hits suddenly and intensely, says Camins. Common symptoms of the flu include: FeverChillsFatigueBody achesRunny noseCoughing It can be difficult to distinguish the signs of a flu infection from those caused by COVID, which is why testing is important, Camins says. If you test positive for influenza, you can seek treatment with antivirals, which can lessen symptom severity and duration. Antivirals are an especially important tool for high-risk groups, including people over the age of 65, children under the age of 5, and immunocompromised individuals. These medications aren’t available over-the-counter, so you’ll need to see a doctor first. “You have to get that prescription fast ... within the first 48 hours after symptom onset, (or else) they don’t work as well,” says Pekosz. If you experience severe flu symptoms, contact your doctor. When to Get the Flu Shot There’s no reason to panic over the mutated H1N1 strain, the experts emphasize, but it is a good reminder to protect yourself. “View (this) as a a sign to go out and get the flu vaccine,” says Pekosz. Getting a flu shot is the most effective way to prevent against severe illness, complications and death from the flu. The 2026-2027 flu vaccines are available at most pharmacies, doctors’ offices and clinics. The updated shots protect against three viruses: influenza A H1N1 (pdm09), influenza A H3N2 and influenza B. There are multiple options available, including standard flu shots, high-dose shots, a nasal mist and the new mRNA flu vaccine. “Even if there’s a mismatched strain, there’s two other strains that the vaccine will provide better protection against,” says Pekosz. Different flu strains can circulate later in the season, so the shot can protect you throughout the winter and early spring. The flu shot is never 100% effective, Camins adds, and you can still get infected if you’ve been vaccinated — but you won’t get nearly as sick or end up in the hospital. Vaccination is especially important if you’re considered high-risk, but everyone can benefit. The best time to get the flu shot is before the end of October, but you can still benefit if you get it later, the experts note. “If you haven’t gotten it yet for whatever reason, now’s the time to get vaccinated because the flu season is starting a little bit sooner and you need at least two weeks for the vaccine immunity to (reach) protective levels,” Pekosz adds. If you aren’t sure which flu vaccine you should get, talk to your doctor or pharmacist.

articles.title: Knee treatment without surgery offers lasting pain relief for 80% of arthritis patients, study finds
articles.summary: A non-surgical knee osteoarthritis treatment uses dissolvable gelatin particles to block excess blood vessels, reducing inflammation without implants, researchers say.
articles.body: A non-surgical procedure that temporarily blocks extra blood vessels in the knee is offering lasting pain relief for people with knee osteoarthritis. In a clinical study of 194 patients, 80% of them reported significant reductions in knee pain that lasted for at least a full year after receiving the treatment. The findings highlight a potential alternative for millions of adults with chronic joint pain who have outgrown pain medications or steroid injections — but who want to avoid total knee replacement. WEIGHT-LOSS DRUGS MAY FIGHT 7 SERIOUS HEALTH PROBLEMS BEFORE THE POUNDS EVEN COME OFF Osteoarthritis wears down joint cartilage and causes the body to grow unnecessary new blood vessels around the knee, according to Mayo Clinic. These extra vessels increase inflammation and irritate surrounding nerves, making daily movement painful. The procedure, known as genicular artery embolization (GAE), addresses this directly. By temporarily clogging excess blood vessels, doctors can reduce inflammation and quiet pain-sensing nerves without major surgery or permanent implants. Because the treatment uses microscopic gelatin particles that dissolve over time, it leaves no foreign material behind. If widely adopted, GAE could provide a repeatable, low-risk way for patients to stay active and preserve joint function longer, researchers say. "We saw a significant drop in pain and a significant increase in function." "For many patients with knee osteoarthritis, there is a real treatment gap today," said Florian Nima Fleckenstein, M.D., deputy head of Interventional Radiology Campus Mitte, Charité-Universitätsmedizin Berlin, in a press release. "Our study demonstrates that GAE using rapidly resorbable gelatin-based microspheres is a safe, minimally invasive therapy that provides meaningful pain relief and functional improvement in participants with osteoarthritis-related knee symptoms for at least 12 months." ALZHEIMER’S RISK LINKED TO COMPOUND FOUND IN POPULAR JOINT HEALTH SUPPLEMENTS During GAE, doctors use real-time X-ray guidance to steer a thin, flexible tube into the blood vessels surrounding the knee joint. Then they release tiny, dissolvable gelatin particles into specific vessels to slow excess blood flow to the inflamed areas. Across 239 total procedures performed on 194 study participants, none experienced severe complications. Only 6.7% reported mild side effects, such as brief skin discoloration or minor bruising, issues that resolved on their own. CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES "In our cohort, we saw a significant drop in pain and a significant increase in function, including sports and recreation and daily activity," Fleckenstein said. "Most importantly, their quality of life significantly increased." CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER In addition to feeling less pain, participants experienced gains in daily mobility. Patients reported easier walking, climbing stairs and bending, while overall quality-of-life scores more than doubled over the 12-month follow-up period. Limitations of study While the results are promising, researchers note several important limitations. First, the study did not include a control group receiving a mock or placebo procedure. Without a comparison group, it is difficult to isolate the physical benefits of the dissolvable particles from potential placebo effects, the researchers said. TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ Second, the study tracked patients for only one year. Further research is needed to determine how long the pain relief typically lasts and how often repeat treatments might be required. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Finally, while GAE effectively reduces inflammation and pain, the researchers said it is not a cure. The procedure does not rebuild lost cartilage or reverse structural joint damage. Larger, randomized trials are currently underway to confirm these early findings. Fox News Digital reached out to the study authors for further comment.

articles.title: Wrestling legend Ric Flair, 77, rushed to Tampa hospital after fall outside bar, head injuries: report
articles.summary: Ric Flair was reportedly rushed to a Tampa hospital by ambulance after falling outside a bar, suffering facial cuts and a possible concussion.
articles.body: Pro wrestling legend Ric Flair was reportedly rushed to a Florida hospital after falling outside a bar. According to TMZ, Flair was at a Tampa bar when he walked outside and fell, injuring his face and possibly suffering a concussion. TMZ says Flair cut his head and eye, which was bleeding, and was loaded into an ambulance. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE The reported fall came hours after Flair announced that he would be unable to attend a scheduled appearance in Seattle due to a blood clot in his leg. "My Doctors Have Limited My Travel To 3–4 Hours. Seattle Falls Outside That Range, And As Disappointed As I Am, I Have To Put My Health And Recovery First. Blood Clots Are Extremely Serious And Can Be Life-Threatening," Flair said on X. "We Have Seen This Recently With Jalen Hurts And The Complications Involving Blood Clots In His Lungs. It Is A Reminder That This Is Not Something To Take Lightly, And I Must Follow Medical Advice." Flair said he is slated to have surgery on the affected vein, "[w]hich My Doctors Expect Will Allow Me To Be Cleared For More Travel Afterward." "Please Know This Decision Was Not Made Lightly. I Am Truly Sorry For The Inconvenience And Disappointment, And I Am Incredibly Grateful For Your Patience, Understanding, And Continued Support. I Look Forward To Getting Healthy And Seeing You All Down The Road. Thank You For The Love And Support," Flair added. Tampa Fire Rescue told OutKick and Fox News Digital that it responded to a fall outside the establishment, and an adult male was taken to a local hospital — the department did not name Flair, saying they could not "provide any patient particulars due to HIPPA guidelines." Flair, 77, has battled health and alcohol issues over the years. EX-WRESTLER PAC'S SUDDEN DEATH CAUSE REVEALED BY COOK COUNTY MEDICAL EXAMINER'S OFFICE Flair has been in and out of wrestling for the last few years. His so-called "Last Match" took place in 2022 — a tag-team match with his then-son-in-law, the wrestler known as Andrade, against Jeff Jarrett and Jay Lethal. He later revealed he passed out twice during the match. Flair made his All Elite Wrestling debut in 2023 and was a brief part of Sting’s final professional match at AEW Revolution, where Sting and Darby Allin took on the Young Bucks. He was a World Championship Wrestling world heavyweight champion eight times, a National Wrestling Alliance world heavyweight champion nine times and a WWE champion twice during his career. articles.title: Vanessa Trump 'finally cancer-free,' she says after health battle in emotional video with daughter Kai
articles.summary: Months after revealing her breast cancer diagnosis in April, Vanessa Trump announces she is cancer-free in an emotional video with daughter Kai Trump.
articles.body: Vanessa Trump revealed she is now cancer-free after battling breast cancer, sharing the emotional health update in a new video with her daughter, Kai Trump, months after publicly announcing her diagnosis. The 19-year-old granddaughter of President Donald Trump shared a preview of the conversation on Instagram during Breast Cancer Awareness Month, revealing that her mother, who's the ex-wife of Donald Trump Jr., was diagnosed in April. "And my mom was diagnosed with breast cancer in April, so we thought we'd share her story and how she was diagnosed, how she overcame it," Kai said in the video. KAI TRUMP REVEALS HOW FAMILY RALLIED AROUND MOM VANESSA AMID BREAST CANCER BATTLE: ‘IT’S A LONG JOURNEY’ To finish the social clip, Vanessa shared the news that she is now cancer-free. "And it came back clear, so I'm finally cancer-free," Vanessa said. "Love you!" Kai responded. The video also features former Fox News medical contributor Dr. Nicole Saphier, who discusses the importance of breast cancer awareness and early detection. "It feels different for everyone," Saphier said. "The reason I like social media talking about breast cancer is because it's reminding people that it is common." In her Instagram caption, Kai said she sat down with her mother and Saphier to discuss Vanessa's cancer journey, prevention and early detection. She also announced that the full conversation would be released on YouTube the following day. Vanessa, the mother of five, first revealed her breast cancer diagnosis in May. "I've recently been diagnosed with breast cancer," Vanessa wrote at the time. "While this isn't news anyone expects, I'm working closely with my medical team on a treatment plan." PRESIDENT'S 19-YEAR-OLD GRANDDAUGHTER, PICTURED IN HOSPITAL AFTER MEDICAL PROCEDURE She revealed that doctors had performed a procedure earlier that week and thanked her family for their support. "I am staying focused and hopeful while surrounded by the love and support of my family, my kids, and those closest to me," she wrote. The announcement prompted support from Ivanka Trump, who wrote, "Praying for your continued strength and a swift recovery. Love you mama." In June, Vanessa said she was recovering from surgery and preparing to begin the second stage of treatment, Fox News Digital reported. Kai Trump later opened up about the emotional experience in an August interview with Fox News Digital, shortly after beginning her freshman year at the University of Miami. CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER "There was definitely, there was a lot of crying in, like, the week leading up," she said of the days before leaving for college. "We would just be driving, and then we'd just start crying together." At the time, she said her mother was improving after treatment. "My mom, she's doing a lot better," she said. "Kind of after treatment, she wasn't feeling very good. Just like how treatment will make you feel … but she's getting a lot better now." Kai described the extra time she spent with her mother over the summer as a "blessing in disguise." "I was able to spend extra time with her that I would normally probably spend on the golf course," Kai said. "It was nice to spend those extra hours with her throughout the day before going to college." CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Now, months after Vanessa first revealed her diagnosis and Kai described their emotional summer together, the mother and daughter are sharing a hopeful new chapter. Fox News Digital's Sophia Compton and Paulina Dedaj contributed reporting.

articles.title: Negligência médica em Guarujá: mãe perde bebê e tem útero retirado | G1
articles.standfirst: Mulher afirma que houve demora no atendimento após a ausência de batimentos cardíacos do bebê ser identificada no hospital em Guarujá (SP). Após o parto, ela também passou por retirada do útero.
articles.summary: A Polícia Civil investiga denúncia de negligência no Hospital Santo Amaro após paciente perder o bebê e ter o útero retirado por demora no atendimento em Guarujá.
articles.body:
Ana Paula Cruz Santos alega negligência durante parto em hospital do Guarujá, SP. — Foto: Arquivo Pessoal

Uma mulher de 37 anos registrou um boletim de ocorrência por suspeita de negligência médica após dar à luz a um bebê natimorto no Hospital Santo Amaro, em Guarujá , no litoral de São Paulo. Ana Paula Cruz Santos alega que houve demora no atendimento após a identificação da ausência de batimentos cardíacos do bebê. Após o parto, ela também teve o útero retirado.

O parto ocorreu na madrugada de terça-feira (20). Ao g1 , Ana Paula contou que, no dia anterior (19), passou por uma consulta de pré-natal de alto risco na Casa Rosa , devido à hipertensão arterial crônica. Segundo ela, estava grávida de oito meses e com a pressão arterial em 17, motivo pelo qual foi encaminhada ao Hospital Santo Amaro. A Polícia Civil investiga o caso.

Segundo o relato, no hospital, a médica que atendeu Ana Paula ouviu os batimentos cardíacos do bebê e administrou um medicamento na veia para aliviar as cólicas. Segundo a mulher, foi solicitada uma ultrassonografia para a manhã seguinte, já que o exame não era realizado naquele horário. Ela também fez exames de sangue e urina, mas foi liberada.

Em nota, a Secretaria de Segurança Pública de São Paulo (SSP-SP) informou que o caso foi registrado como morte natural na Delegacia de Polícia de Guarujá, que requisitou exame pericial ao Instituto Médico Legal (IML) para esclarecimento dos fatos.

Procurado, o Hospital Santo Amaro não se posicionou sobre o caso até a última atualização desta reportagem.

De acordo com o relato, as dores aumentaram depois que chegou em casa e, por isso, voltou ao hospital por volta das 19h, acompanhada da mãe. Segundo ela, o médico que a atendeu tentou ouvir os batimentos do bebê, mas não conseguiu. A mulher afirmou que continuou sentindo fortes dores enquanto aguardava os resultados dos exames e passava por outros procedimentos.

“Ele colocou o aparelho na minha barriga e não escutou o coração do neném. [...] O que ele tinha que ter feito de imediato era uma cesárea de emergência”, disse ela.

Ana Paula contou que permaneceu no hospital durante a noite e que, por volta das 3h, começou a sangrar ao tentar ir ao banheiro . Em seguida, foi encaminhada para uma cesárea de emergência, mas o bebê nasceu morto.

Ana Paula disse que sofreu uma hemorragia e precisou receber transfusões de sangue. Ela também afirmou que teve seu útero retirado após a cesárea, o que a impossibilita de engravidar novamente. A mulher atribui o ocorrido à assistência recebida no hospital.

“Eu não tô conseguindo processar tudo isso, acabou para mim. Quem me conhece sabe que o sonho da minha vida era ser mãe. Está doendo demais o que fizeram comigo. Eu não vou poder ter filho mais e mataram meu filho”, disse.

Ana Paula relatou que tenta lidar com a perda do bebê e com a impossibilidade de ter outros filhos. “Meu peito enche de leite e eu não tenho filho para amamentar. Eu sinto o meu bebê mexer lá dentro, mas não tem bebê nenhum. Eu fiz uma cesárea e não tenho criança. Eles acabaram com o sonho da minha vida inteira de ter um filho”, afirmou.
